question.worked_solution:
Solving $x+y+z=0$ for $z,$ we get $z=-x-y.$ Solving $2x-y-w=0$ for $w,$ we get $w=2x-y.$  Therefore, any vector from $\text{Ker}(T)$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ 2x-y \\ -x-y\end{aligned}]=x{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{v}_{1}}+y{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{v}_{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

This means that $\text{Ker}(T)=\text{Span}\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\}.$ Therefore, $\text{nullity}(T)=2.$ 

Finally, according the rank-nullity theorem, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{rank}(T) & =4-\text{nullity}(T) \\  & =4-2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
